notes: SCOPE (screen step, 1 sample). Paths are relative to showcase/runs/night-cartridge/1.2.0-rc.6/<app>/20261018-024608/. Published evidence is 1.1.0-rc.2/<app>/20261015-034853/. It no longer reads as a bucket or padlock. Residual, low, caused by the spec's grid: the sides step outward below mid-height, so the shape leans toward a lunch box or cooler. It reads as a bag next to the 'Bags' label and beside the day pack and duffel. (2) Visible-ink sprite size 40–50%: FIXED. Grid 41–44%, detail 46% at 1440 and about 48% at 390 (see MEASUREMENTS). PROCESS (every app of this sample, so recurring by the rubric; not scored, since it does not change the output people see). The report's computed tables are 'not written' in 4 of 4 apps, despite rc.6's 'not written fails it' rule. Commerce says the full tables 'are not written out here' (agent-report.md line 37). Settings: 'I didn't write out the full per-scene tables' (line 32). Dashboard: 'I couldn't produce the spec's computed scene and sprite tables, because I'm limited to the five allowed commands and can't run a script' (line 34). The blog report has no per-scene table. The cause is the environment, not wording: the run's allowed commands do not include a script runner, so pct() and the scene checks cannot run. Every agent still measured on a temporary close-up page, and the visible measurements pass. Also from the reports: the review routes were left behind as empty files that the agents could not delete (commerce src/pages/ReviewPage.tsx, blog and settings src/pages/ArtReview.tsx).

COMPARED WITH PUBLISHED 1.1.0. Everything rc.5 lost is back: full summaries, category icons and the two-column settings form. Banner leads are 111–119px against about 117px. The tote, sprite sizes, hero and scene variety are better than published. Nothing I opened is worse than 1.1.0.

SIGNATURE (4). Present in all four apps and placed as Applying says. Blog home has a full-bleed hero with a framed title window, a lit post office on a rimmed rise, a diagonal path, moon, stars and drifting clouds. Each article and the about page has its own banner with a distinct lead, and the article body uses inline scene images (posts-shipping-a-design-system-desktop-light.png, the 'inventory board' figure). The store grid, cart and every product page have strips or banners with their own leads (SHOP, SHIP, TOTE). Dashboard and settings have one strip per screen (a server yard; a workshop with a gear plate, a fuse house and a PAY depot). Empty states have vignettes (blog state-search-empty, dashboard state-empty-filter), and the checkered ground strip runs everywhere. Motion is stepped. motion-m1.png shows nc-drift at 120000ms with steps(40), and the cloud moves between frames; the nav marker blinks; keyframes are swap, drift, sparkle, blink, twinkle and rare (blog shots.json). Grid sprites are now 41–44% visible ink and read as their products. Why not 5: the tote's step-out sides lean toward a lunch box (B); props in the store and dashboard strips are small and sparse, at the reference strip's scale but with less craft than the reference's tree and figure detail (commerce/drawings/home-d1.png vs reference/illustrations/p2-i2.png); product banners repeat one building type per category (A).

OTHER SCORES. Reference fidelity (4): a night ground, cream pixel type, 4px windows, dither rules under h2s, one gold commit with a hard shadow, the gold ▶ marker, hue top bars and bullets, block meters and the checkered grass strip, as in reference/screenshots/p1-desktop-light.png, without its cabin, figure or snow. Cross-app consistency (4): one family in all four apps. Dashboard and settings both use a sidebar shell; blog and commerce use top navigation, as their kinds allow. Hierarchy (4): scene and h1 first, then ruled h2s; the 48px KPIs lead the dashboard; the 48px price and gold Add to cart lead the product page; blog summaries are readable again. Spacing (4): the 4px scale and h2 rhythm hold; panels end level; the settings form fills its window. The soft spots are the tall detail picture window (C) and the dashboard filter row (D), each seen once. Component states (4): a gold focus frame on the invalid field, danger frames with '!' messages (settings state-profile-errors-desktop-light.png; commerce state-checkout-errors-desktop-light.png); a titled dialog with a framed close, Cancel and gold Confirm (settings state-plan-dialog-desktop-light.png); empty results with a vignette, a 0-of-n meter and a framed Clear filters (blog state-search-empty, dashboard state-empty-filter). Polish (4): radius 0, 2/4px borders, no default-browser leftovers, and no generic look.

BAR: seven 4s, average 4.0, none below 3. The screen PASSES and the candidate should go on to the confirm step (2 more samples). Update goal: reached in this sample. All seven rc.5 recurring findings are FIXED, and every earlier tracked item is FIXED. The only recurring problem is process: the computed report tables are absent in 4 of 4 apps because the run environment cannot run scripts. It does not change the output people see and is not scored. Watch in the confirm samples: the tote's step-out sides, sameness across commerce product banners, and the visible ink of the 20-visible-unit sprites (41–42% here, close to the floor).
